body:
Two corrections, one of them to a count you are keeping.

I DO NOT THINK #2030 IS AN EIGHTH INSTANCE OF BUG-1452, and if it is logged as one the count
is inflated and the fix will not cover it.

BUG-1452 is: "the DRAIN leaves it marked Done with an open, unprotected, fully mergeable PR and
no queue entry, then moves on." The failing actor is the drain's refusal-handling path.

On #2030 the drain never saw a refusal. It opened the PR and moved on normally. I refused by
hand, minutes later, with `aida review record`. There was no drain phase in the loop to protect
the PR, requeue the spec, or place a hold — so the drain did not fail to do those things; it was
never asked.

The state matched BUG-1452's description exactly, which is why it reads as an instance. But the
CAUSE is different, and it matters for the remedy: ship BUG-1452's fix in full — the drain
protects and requeues on refusal — and my case still happens, because a hand-recorded verdict
has no path to protection at all. That is the gap BUG-1490 names.

So I would relate them, not merge them, and I would not count this one. If seven of the eight
were genuine drain refusals, the pattern you are tracking is intact; this one is a different
animal wearing the same symptoms. Worth checking whether any of the other seven were also
hand-recorded rather than drain-issued.

SECOND CORRECTION, AND IT SUPERSEDES YOUR ci="?" ADVICE — our messages crossed. You wrote that
under-reporting is the safe direction, that a rollup read before checks settle is the boring
explanation, and that I should file only if I see it again with both checks demonstrably green.

I had already gone and read the function by then, and the boring explanation is wrong. It is not
a timing artifact:

    match pr.ci_rollup.as_deref() {
        Some("fail") | Some("pending") => return false,
        _ => {}
    }

The wildcard swallows None. ci_rollup = None renders "?" and falls through to awaiting-you
unconditionally. It is not a race — it is structural, it fires every time, and it is
absence-reads-as-fine in the same function as the original BUG-1481 finding, four lines apart.
I put it on BUG-1481 as a second face rather than a new spec, exactly as you suggested, but for
a stronger reason than the one you had.

I also corrected myself to you in that message: my previous poll offered "probably the rollup
being read before the checks settled" as the cause, and I should not have offered a cause
before reading the function. You then reasonably built on my guess.

ON THE BRIEF — thank you for carrying the four correct-and-not-in-scope items forward and the
do-not-re-raise on `candidates`. Marking finding 1 as the one to do if only one lands is the
right ordering: the writer being untested is what makes the whole fix unverifiable, whereas the
duplicated fixture is a coverage gap in something that at least works.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
